title: selectedDate never advances at local midnight while the tab stays open
setup: Test athlete, Fuel tab open on /fuel (Nutrition sub-tab), tagged rows only (OVN-fuel-r1-01).
steps: 1. Load /fuel at 23:55 local (use page.clock to set the browser clock). 2. Leave the tab open, do not reload or navigate. 3. Advance page.clock past local midnight to 00:10 the next day. 4. Tap 'Add' → manual entry → food_name 'OVN-fuel-r1-01 midnight snack', calories 100 → Add Food (no reload, no date-picker interaction).
expected: Either the day rolls over automatically (entry lands on the new date) or the UI visibly shows 'yesterday' so the athlete knows which day they're logging to. Silently logging a post-midnight entry to the stale date with no indicator would misattribute it in the daily/weekly totals.
risk: src/pages/FoodTracker.jsx:202 — selectedDate = useState(format(new Date(), 'yyyy-MM-dd')) initializes once on mount and never re-derives from a live clock; the write at :1104 uses date: selectedDate.
serializeReason: writes a row to the shared account's day total for 'today'/'yesterday'; must not overlap another attacker logging to the same dates.

title: 'Logging earlier' eaten_at across a DST fall-back transition
setup: Test athlete, America/Denver profile timezone. Tagged rows (OVN-fuel-r1-02).
steps: 1. Use page.clock to set the date to 2026-11-01 (the Sunday DST falls back in America/Denver). 2. Tap 'Add' → toggle 'Logging earlier' → meal type 'dinner' (default clock time 19:00 per MEAL_DEFAULT_TIME) → food_name 'OVN-fuel-r1-02 dst dinner', calories 500 → Add Food, with selectedDate = 2026-11-01. 3. Read back the created row's eaten_at (query food_entries filtered to this tagged row) and confirm which UTC instant it resolved to.
expected: eaten_at should represent 19:00 local on 2026-11-01 regardless of the DST transition, i.e. a consistent UTC offset for that specific date/time, not silently using the wrong pre/post-DST offset from a stale cached offset.
risk: src/pages/FoodTracker.jsx:73-77 getEatenAt — new Date(`${dateStr}T${time}:00`).toISOString() relies on the browser's current local-to-UTC conversion for that specific date string; confirm it's using the date's own offset and not a globally cached one.

expected: Ring and macro bars render a sane number (treating null as 0 contribution) with no NaN/blank/-- displayed anywhere, and the ring's calorie total still includes the 320 kcal.
risk: src/utils/nutritionUtils.js:8-24 calculateMacros uses (entry.protein_grams || 0) etc., which is null-safe; verify the ring SVG math (FoodTracker.jsx:1737-1761, the overflow arc) and intakeStats memo (:1510-1561) don't independently re-derive these fields without the same null guard.

title: Serving amount of 0.00001 passes validation and logs a near-zero-calorie ghost entry
steps: 1. Tap 'Add' → USDA search 'chicken breast' → select a generic result. 2. In the serving-amount field (min="0" step="0.5", FoodTracker.jsx:2807), clear it and type '0.00001'. 3. Tap 'Add Food' (submit only rejects <= 0, FoodTracker.jsx:3145).
expected: Either the UI rejects/clamps a serving amount that rounds to an unusable quantity, or it's accepted and the resulting calories/macros round sensibly to 0 without a phantom entry that inflates the day's item count for no nutritional signal.
risk: src/pages/FoodTracker.jsx:2807 (input min/step, no upper or granularity floor) and :3145 (disabled check is `(parseFloat(newFood.serving_amount) || 0) <= 0`, which lets 0.00001 through since it's > 0).
serializeReason: writes a food_entries row counted in today's shared totals.

title: 10000 g portion on a manual entry — do macros scale linearly with no sanity cap
steps: 1. Tap 'Add' → USDA search 'almonds' → select a generic 100 g result (~579 kcal/100g). 2. Change serving unit to grams, type '10000' into the amount field. 3. Tap 'Add Food'.
expected: A 10 kg serving of almonds (~57,900 kcal) is either flagged/blocked as an implausible entry before saving, or at minimum doesn't corrupt the day's ring (e.g. break the SVG arc math, produce a negative 'remaining' display that reads as a UI glitch rather than 'way over').
risk: src/pages/FoodTracker.jsx:2807 no upper bound on serving amount; ring overflow-arc code at :1748-1758 — confirm it degrades gracefully (visually caps/labels overflow) rather than rendering a broken arc for a 50x-over-target day.
serializeReason: massively skews today's shared calorie total for anyone else reading it in the same window; delete immediately after assertion.

title: Double-tap Delete on a food entry — no isPending guard, no confirm, no undo
setup: Test athlete, one tagged food entry already logged today (OVN-fuel-r1-06).
steps: 1. Create the tagged entry via the Add flow. 2. Locate its row and fire two near-simultaneous clicks on its Trash icon (FoodTracker.jsx:2222) before the first request's response returns (simulate with two click() calls back-to-back, no await between them).
expected: Exactly one entry is removed, no error surfaces, no crash, and the day's totals reflect the single removal. Per judge rules, a destructive action with no undo is itself worth flagging even if the double-tap doesn't corrupt data — confirm there really is zero recovery path (no 'Entry deleted' toast Undo action).
risk: src/pages/FoodTracker.jsx:1120-1128 deleteFoodMutation has no onError handler and the trash button at :2222 has no disabled={deleteFoodMutation.isPending} guard (contrast with addFoodMutation at :3145, which does).
serializeReason: mutates a shared-account row; run this case alone so no other attacker is mid-write on the same entry.

steps: 1. Ensure a tagged planned row exists for today. 2. Fire two near-simultaneous clicks on its 'mark as eaten' checkbox (FoodTracker.jsx:2143, togglePlannedMutation :1132-1141) before the first mutation's response returns.

title: Edit an entry's amount, reload before the update lands

title: Offline manual add — form state preserved for retry, no false success
setup: Test athlete, Fuel tab open, no existing tagged rows.
steps: 1. context.setOffline(true). 2. Tap 'Add' → manual entry → food_name 'OVN-fuel-r1-09 offline test', calories 200 → tap 'Add Food'. 3. Observe the toast/error and whether the dialog stays open with the typed values intact. 4. context.setOffline(false), tap 'Add Food' again.
expected: Offline attempt shows a clear failure toast ('Failed to log food', FoodTracker.jsx:1116) and does NOT show a false 'Food logged successfully!' success. The typed form values must still be present after the failed attempt (resetForm() only runs onSuccess, :1112) so the athlete doesn't have to retype. Once back online, the retry succeeds and exactly one entry is created (not zero, not two).
risk: src/pages/FoodTracker.jsx:1091-1118 addFoodMutation onError (:1115-1117) — confirm the dialog does not close and no optimistic entry appears in the day's list while offline.
serializeReason: eventually writes a tagged row to today's shared total once reconnected.

title: Re-approve the week plan after manually editing one planned item's amount
setup: Test athlete, week plan already approved (from fuel-r1-10 or a fresh approve). Tag any manual edit distinctly.
steps: 1. Approve the week plan once. 2. Edit one of today's planned entries (tap it → change serving amount, e.g. double it → Save Changes). 3. Reopen the Week plan dialog and tap 'Approve & load the week' again. 4. Check whether the hand-edited entry survived or was silently overwritten.
expected: Either re-approving warns that it will discard manual edits to already-loaded planned items, or it's documented/expected behavior — but a silent, unannounced overwrite of a user's manual correction is a data-loss-adjacent UX bug worth flagging per judge rules ('entered data is never lost').
risk: src/components/nutrition/WeeklyPlanCard.jsx:214-225 — approve deletes ALL existing planned:true rows for the week's dates unconditionally before recreating from resolveDayPlan(), with no diff against rows the user has since hand-edited.
